classification.difficultyReason: Calculate floor and tile areas, then divide and cancel the common squared pronumeral.

content.prompt: A floor of a room is rectangular in shape, has length $10x$ metres and width $7x$ metres. The floor is to be tiled with rectangular tiles each of length $\frac{x}{3}$ metres and width $\frac{x}{4}$ metres. How many tiles are needed to tile this floor area?

answer.short:
$840$ tiles.

Divide the floor area by the area of one tile.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{floor}}&=10x\times7x\\A_{\text{floor}}&=70x^2\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{tile}}&=\frac{x}{3}\times\frac{x}{4}\\A_{\text{tile}}&=\frac{x^2}{12}\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$

The number of tiles is the floor area divided by the area of one tile.

$$\begin{align*}N&=70x^2\div\frac{x^2}{12}\\N&=\frac{70x^2\times12}{x^2}\\N&=840\end{align*}$$

$840$ tiles are needed.
